title: Training & appraisal
examples: What is the difference between training and appraisal?
Can you give an example of off-the-job training?
How does an appraisal help an employee?

explain.say: Today we will learn about training and appraisal in a business setting. These help employees grow in their jobs.
First we look at on-the-job training. This means learning while doing the actual job tasks. For example, a new shop assistant learns by helping a senior worker.
Next we study off-the-job training. This happens away from the normal workplace tasks. For instance, a manager might attend a workshop on leadership skills.
Now we move to performance appraisals. This is a formal review of an employee's work and progress. For example, a yearly review might discuss sales targets achieved.
In real life, a dentist might undergo training on new X-ray equipment. This is off-the-job learning. Then, the dentist's practice might conduct an appraisal to check their patient care skills.
A common mistake is thinking that training only happens when someone fails. Remember, training is also for improving skills before problems happen. You should see it as continuous improvement.

draw.text: Mistake: Thinking training is only for failure

faq.q: What is the main difference between the two types of training?
faq.a: On-the-job training happens while you are doing your actual job tasks. Off-the-job training happens in a separate place like a classroom.
asks: Does off-the-job training mean I leave work?

faq.q: What is the purpose of a performance appraisal?
faq.a: The appraisal helps both the employee and the employer see where improvements are needed. It sets goals for the future development.
asks: Is appraisal just about pointing out mistakes?
What does the company get from appraisals?

faq.a: No, appraisals can discuss areas for improvement, but they should also acknowledge successes. They are balanced reviews.
asks: Can I argue during an appraisal?
What if my manager is unfair?

faq.q: Do I need to ask for training myself?
faq.a: Yes, it is good to show initiative by asking about courses or skills you want to learn. This shows commitment to the role.
asks: How do I ask for more training?

faq.q: Is formal training always better than informal learning?
faq.a: Neither is always better; they are different. Formal training is structured, while informal learning happens naturally on the job.

facts: On-the-job training uses the workplace environment for learning.
Off-the-job training might involve external courses or seminars.
Appraisals are formal reviews of job performance and progress.
Both training and appraisals aim to improve employee skills.

quiz.say: Learning how to use a new piece of accounting software while working on real accounts is an example of:
quiz.why: This learning happens using the actual tools and tasks of the job.

wrong.0: This suggests the learning happened in a separate classroom setting.
wrong.1: An appraisal is a review, not the act of learning a skill.
wrong.2: This term is too general and does not specify the work context.

quiz.say: A manager attending a seminar on improving team communication is an example of:
quiz.why: Attending a seminar means the learning takes place away from the main office tasks.

wrong.0: This implies the learning was done while managing the team at the office.
wrong.1: An appraisal is a review, not the act of attending a seminar.
wrong.2: This describes testing skills, not the initial learning from a seminar.

quiz.say: If a company reviews an employee's sales figures from the last quarter against set targets, they are conducting a:
quiz.why: Reviewing past performance against goals is the core function of an appraisal.

wrong.0: Training is about teaching skills, not measuring past results.
wrong.1: A task is the work itself, not the formal review of that work.
wrong.2: A workshop is a learning event, not a formal review meeting.
